rv.q: I wouldn't say the pair on the stage of the Raven Theatre manifest a similar energy, even though they're both fine, sexy actors. They just don't ever really feel connected.
In Simon Stephens’ tightly constructed one-act, it actually works.
Under the direction of Nate Cohen, Scott Anderson and Laura Coover star in Griffin Theatre’s Chicago premiere of this quietly profound two-hander.
Heisenberg is an entertaining 90 minutes but there are a few bumps in the road, most of them problems with the script rather than the staging or performances.

"Heisenberg” isn’t exactly a bad play: it’s just a thin, slow-moving one, driven by a male ambivalence about women that portrays the female protagonist less as a human being than a kind of shape-shifting femme fatale.
To say that this production falls short is an understatement.

cn.t: Simon Stephens' two-hander receives a mixed response, with critics divided on whether strong performances can overcome a chaotic, uneven script that some find captivating while others deem confused and overly hysterical.
